question: Why do language models operate on tokens rather than raw characters?
options: Tokens compress sequences and balance vocabulary size against sequence length
Characters are too computationally expensive to store
It's a hardware limitation of GPUs

question: Which of the following is true about modern subword tokenizers like BPE?
options: Common words are usually a single token; rare words are split into multiple subword pieces
Each token always corresponds to exactly one English word
Tokens correspond one-to-one with Unicode code points

question: If a vocabulary has 50,000 tokens, what does the model output at each step before sampling?
options: A 50,000-dimensional vector of logits, one per possible next token
The token id of the next word as a single integer
A binary yes/no for each token
